text:
With Nathan MacKinnon sidelined, The Hockey Writers framed it as a test for Martin Necas, and he's mostly passed. He has 29 points in 24 games, including a goal and two assists against Montreal on Nov. 25, and he shook off a scary hit against Utah on Nov. 18.

The finishing is ahead of the chances. He has 11 goals on 6.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 20% against 18% last season, and Colorado has scored 5.8 more goals than expected with him on the ice. His ice time has dipped lately too, to 19 minutes a night. What is not a fluke is the skating and the playmaking: NHL Edge counts 98 bursts over 20 mph, 99th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 95th percentile for primary shot assists last season. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 11th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, though with strong teammates. Our numbers project about 94 points. Watch what he creates without MacKinnon feeding him.
headline: Necas carries Colorado without MacKinnon
